html:
SMTO-SKL-0005 — This Skill needs the name of a saved secret, not the secret itself

GUID: fd2cc944-171d-45b0-aed2-33aaf8a008b7
Slug: skill-secret-reference-required
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: skl

What happened

  • Skills keep API keys in Parameter Store, SMTO's protected place for secrets. This setting was filled in incorrectly or names a Parameter Store entry that doesn't exist, so your changes weren't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and make sure an entry holding the API key exists. If it doesn't, create one and save it. Skill settings only point to secrets; the secret itself has to live in Parameter Store.
  2. In the Skill's settings window, type that entry's exact name in Parameter Store key. SMTO doesn't match similar names, so the name must be exactly right.
  3. In Credential field pointer, type a slash followed by the name of the field inside the entry that holds the key. Never paste the key itself here. This tells SMTO which part of the entry is the key while keeping the key hidden.
  4. Select Save. SMTO checks that the entry and field exist before it saves.

What success looks like

  • The settings window says "Saved. Future calls use this configuration."

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the API key into the Skill settings or the conversation; it would no longer be protected.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Skill configuration secret_reference field is not a valid CredentialReference (parameter_key of 1–160 characters plus a JSON Pointer starting with /), or on save no Parameter Store record exists under that exact normalized key.

What this means

  • A secret field fails CredentialReference validation, or configuration saving cannot resolve the exact named Parameter Store record. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A secret field fails CredentialReference validation, or configuration saving cannot resolve the exact named Parameter Store record.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect parameter_key and pointer structure and exact entry existence without revealing the value.

How to fix it

  • Store the credential in Parameter Store, then set the field's parameter_key to that entry's exact key and pointer to a JSON Pointer for the string field (starting with /); the editor's "Parameter Store key" and "Credential field pointer" inputs map to these. SkillConfigurationStore._check_references requires the record to exist under the same normalized key. Never put the raw secret in the configuration.
  • Store the credential in Parameter Store and provide a valid exact entry/field reference; restore a missing referenced entry when necessary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The public configuration stores a valid reference to the intended existing secret field.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
